uncertain.text: ſcrutables iugemẽs de la diuinité) plaiſans, ny agreables
uncertain.note: the sign after 'diuinité' is not the curved ) of this fount (compare 'exemple)' two lines below): it is a single straight oblique stroke, x-height and above, leaning top-left to bottom-right like a backslash. Syntax requires the closing bracket of the parenthesis opened at 'eſtre(', so it is transcribed as ')'; it is probably a battered or turned parenthesis. Could alternatively be a virgule set upside down.

uncertain.text: ſcrutables iugemẽs de la diuinité) plaiſans, ny agreables
uncertain.note: the mark over the e of 'iugemẽs' is a thick, near-horizontal, slightly wavy bar, quite unlike the thin steep acute on 'diuinité' in the same line (checked side by side at 12x). Read as a tilde: iugemẽs = iugemens. Reading 'iugemés' cannot be excluded.

uncertain.text: Dieu: & moins la fin, pour laquelle ce ſainct & venerable
uncertain.note: a small round mark sits on the baseline between 'ſainct' and '&'. It is clearly smaller than this fount's full stops (compare the point in 'Dieu:' at the head of the line) and touches the foot of the t, so it is treated as an ink speck / part of the ct and omitted. If it is a full stop the line reads 'ce ſainct. & venerable'.

uncertain.text: quelquefois laſcher la bride trop lõgue à leurs affectiõs
uncertain.note: two small dots stand above the first a of 'affectiõs', looking like a diaeresis. They are lighter than the type and irregularly spaced; read as ink specks or a rising space, so the a is transcribed plain.

uncertain.text: deſordonnées. Ie preuoy biẽ ici, qu'on m'oppoſera ie ne
uncertain.note: a small raised tick, shaped like an apostrophe, stands between 'm'oppoſera' and 'ie'. It is not a marker letter (all markers on this page are italic a-f) and the sense needs nothing there, so it is omitted as a stray sort or speck.

the figure is a hooked stroke with no dot above it, unlike every italic i on the page (compare 'frigid', 'quicquid'), and the notes use arabic figures elsewhere ('au 6.', 'L. 2.', '& 3.'). Read as arabic 1. The same glyph occurs at margin_notes[1].lines[1] ('1. & canõ qui') and margin_notes[3].lines[0] ('Loy 1. ſur'); all three could be roman i.
the point between 'ii' and 'au' is faint and low; it may be a comma or nothing at all. Transcribed as a full stop by analogy with 'xxxii. q. ii.' in note c and 'ri xxii. q. v.' in note d.

the compositor sets many word pairs tight ('par lesloix', 'onvoid', 'nede mille', 'deMariage', 'leMariage', 'delicesdu') and sets the round brackets hard against the neighbouring word ('eſtre(s'il', '&(comme', 'exemple)plei', 'diuinité)plaiſans', 'monde.a(qui', 'precipiter c)mais'). Per conventions §1 the compositor's spacing is not reproduced, so all of these are transcribed with a single ordinary word space, which is also what scripts/validate_page.py enforces.
set in widely letterspaced capitals like the running head above it, hence spaced_caps. The final I. is a roman numeral one, printed as a capital I with a full stop.
